summary: Benchmarked the residue-reachability DP for N=M^2 (p<=3000, m in [50,999], 300 cases) with a Python set, a Python-int bitset (per-bit gather) and numpy gather; all three gave identical sets. The bitset gave no speedup (set 4 ms total, bigint 25 ms, numpy 13 ms), because multiplication by a residue is not a shift; bit-parallel rotation only helps the additive analogue. The reachable sets are small (median |R|/m = 0.09, max 0.99), so this is mainly a small-set benchmark.
not_done: No large-set benchmark (|R| close to m); no C/SIMD bitset implementation.
next: None for ES; bit-parallel gather would need a C implementation with |R|~m to be assessed.

summary: Full pair-completion search over Z[ζ8] with coefficient height ≤2 for x,y (z unrestricted), n ≤ 200: 27,974 pair completions with integral z over 77 n-values; sampled hits verified exactly (sympy). Premise issue: the cone 'totally positive relative norm to K⁺' is automatic (x·x̄ is totally positive in Q(√2) for every nonzero x), and K is totally imaginary, so denominators cannot be totally real-positive; the unit-only test (72 units, |k|≤4) gives solutions only at n=4 (trivial). Height ≤30 is beyond the cap: the element count scales (61/5)^4 ≈ 2·10⁴, pair count ~5·10⁸.
not_done: Height 30 (cost, above); the cone condition has no non-trivial reading for K totally imaginary.

summary: Macbeath-type check (scripts/z52d_p2_NC0_Z0154.py): for each ES triple (x,y,z) of 4/n, n=5..40, and q∈{5,7,11,13}, searched for a generating pair A,B∈PSL(2,q) with ord(A)|x, ord(B)|y, ord(AB)|z (generation checked by BFS). A generating quotient was found for every n in 5..40 (for some q). The check does not discriminate: the groups are small, so many triples admit quotients. Riemann–Hurwitz integrality (n | 4|G| for a torsion-free kernel of index |G|) holds only for small q and fails for most large prime n, so no large-n quotient was tested.
not_done: Quotients with q ≥ 17 or PGL/other groups; torsion-free kernel check; hard primes n ≡ 1 (mod 840) (not in range). Earlier draft accepted trivial pairs (A=B=1); corrected by requiring generation.
next: Check whether PSL(2,q) quotients with q ~ n^{1/3} exist for the hard primes via Macbeath's signature conditions instead of brute force.

summary: PROVED: pairwise-coprime ES denominators are impossible (x | n·yz with gcd(x,yz)=1 forces xyz | n, and then 4 = m(xy+yz+zx) has no solution). Milnor–Orlik (checked on A2, A4, E6, E8 and Ẽ8 links) for all 9,438 unordered ES triples with n ≤ 120: Σc_k is even, ≥2, and never 0 (range 2–126). So Δ(t) vanishes at t=1 for every ES triple, the link is never a rational homology sphere, and its H_1 is infinite (b_1 ≥ 1 by the Milnor/Brieskorn correspondence, not checked against a source).
not_done: H_1 torsion (finite part) not computed: H_1 is infinite for every triple. Milnor–Orlik sum vs b_1 not checked against a source.
next: Compare Σc_k − 2 with the Seifert base genus of Σ(x,y,z) (Neumann–Raymond) to make b_1 explicit.

summary: Lattice width of conv(all integer solution points) for 12 primes (directions |u_i|≤6): 9 (p=5), 408 (13), 420 (17), 1.15e6 (101), 7.97e6 (409), 4.67e8 (577), 1.97e9 (1009), 9.18e10 (3361), 5.06e11 (5569), 9.73e10 (9601), 2.66e14 (23929), 7.07e15 (83449); the widths are of the same order as the largest solution coordinate, so the hull is never flat.
